item.title: Cognitive Phase Transitions
item.description:
Why talk about usefulness?

When we discuss intelligent systems, being enthusiastic about usefulness seems overly utilitarian, cold, and harsh — meritocratic, lacking humanistic care. But refusing to talk about usefulness at all, being evasive about objectively measuring human intelligence and LLMs, is even more a form of cowardice.

Whether LLMs are conscious, whether subjective experience can arise from silicon-based computation or even from abstract computation — these propositions cannot be answered and are unknowable.

item.title: Reflecting on a Wake-up
item.description:
In the half-awake state, while my memory of the waking process was still fresh, I hurried to record some thoughts and insights as follows:

The human body is a physical computer — just like thermodynamic computers and quantum computers.

Sleep is the suspension of consciousness.

In the moment between sleep and waking, the neural network is gradually activated.

Dreams are essentially the product of not-yet-fully-online logical capacity working on memory at the moment the power first comes on.
